title: Design a Logging Framework
relevance: High — classic LLD / machine-coding round that packs Chain of Responsibility, Strategy, Singleton/Factory, Observer-style fan-out, and concurrency into one problem; asked at Uber, Google, Atlassian, Amazon, and many Indian product cos.
company_notes: Campus/new-grad machine-coding or LLD in India (Amazon, Flipkart, Uber, Walmart, Atlassian-style): working console+file logger with levels and a clear class diagram. SDE-2 probes hierarchy/additivity, async backpressure, per-appender levels, MDC, lock granularity, Log4j/SLF4J comparison. FAANG OOD whiteboard emphasizes clarifying questions and pattern naming. Standard LLD set piece for Chain of Responsibility plus concurrency.

phases.goal: Clarify in-process library scope, mandatory FRs/NFRs, and what to defer as optional extensions.

must_hit.point: Scope as an in-process logging library (Log4j/SLF4J-style), not a distributed aggregator; call out async, hierarchy, rotation, and remote sinks as optional extensions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate asks library vs Kafka→ELK aggregator and states the interview wants the library, with advanced features optional.

must_hit.point: Mandatory FR: log at DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR/FATAL; each record has timestamp, level, and message; configurable min level; write to console and/or file; extensible for new destinations.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists levels, record fields, threshold config, console/file sinks, and extensibility for new destinations.

must_hit.point: NFR: thread-safe (no interleaved lines), low overhead when a level is disabled, OCP for new sinks/formats, and a simple client API like logger.info.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names thread-safety, disabled-level short-circuit, OCP, and a clean info/debug-style API.

must_hit.point: Common extensions to ask about: multiple appenders, custom formatters (plain/JSON), async path, named hierarchical loggers with additivity, Database/Kafka appender, rolling files, MDC.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Proactively lists multi-appender, formatters, async, hierarchy/additivity, remote sinks, rolling files, and MDC as ask-first extensions.

probes: Is this an in-process library or a distributed log aggregator, and which features are in v1 vs optional?
What must every log record include, and which destinations are mandatory for the first cut?

hints.1: Start by asking library vs aggregator before listing features.
hints.2: Separate mandatory FR (levels, console/file, min level) from optional FR (async, hierarchy, Kafka).
hints.3: State: in-process library; DEBUG…FATAL; timestamp+level+message; console and/or file; thread-safe; OCP; async/hierarchy as extensions.

phases.goal: Identify the core data objects and how log events and levels are modeled.

must_hit.point: Log levels are an ordered enum TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR < FATAL; emit only if messageLevel >= configuredLevel.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows an ordered level enum and a >= threshold rule for emission.

must_hit.point: LogMessage (or LogRecord) is an immutable event carrying level, message, timestamp, logger name, and optionally thread name.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes an immutable LogMessage with those fields built after the level check.

must_hit.point: Optional LoggerConfig holds min level and the list of appenders rather than hardcoding setup inside log().
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions a config object or factory setup for min level and appenders at startup.

probes: What fields belong on a LogMessage, and when is it created relative to the level check?
How do you represent log levels so threshold filtering is a simple comparison?

hints.1: Think enum for levels and a single event object for each log call.
hints.2: Level check first, then allocate the immutable LogMessage.
hints.3: Ordered enum TRACE…FATAL; LogMessage(level, message, timestamp, loggerName, threadName?); optional LoggerConfig(minLevel, appenders).

phases.goal: Sketch Logger, LogManager, Appender/Formatter strategies, hierarchy, and pattern roles.

must_hit.point: LogManager/LoggerFactory is a Singleton registry of named Loggers via getLogger(name)—not a single Singleton Logger for the whole app.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws LogManager.getLogger(name) returning named loggers from a registry.

must_hit.point: Compose Formatter and Appender independently (Strategy): Console/File/DB appenders each use a LogFormatter (plain or JSON)—avoid JsonFileAppender × PlainConsoleAppender explosion.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows LogAppender uses LogFormatter; same formatter works across destinations.

must_hit.point: Logger fans out to a list of LogAppenders (Observer-style); hierarchy uses parent Logger for effective level and additivity/propagate bubble-up (production CoR), not an INFO→DEBUG→ERROR handler class chain.
must_hit.evidence_hint: List of appenders for fan-out; parent pointer + getEffectiveLevel and additivity; contrasts with the teaching-only level-handler chain.

must_hit.point: AsyncAppender Decorator wraps another Appender; Template Method shape is filter → format → emit on the handler path.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Decorator for async wrapper and the filter/format/emit skeleton.

probes: Why is Singleton on Logger a junior smell, and what should own the registry instead?
How do hierarchy CoR and list-of-appenders differ from an INFO→DEBUG→ERROR handler chain?

hints.1: Name Strategy, Observer fan-out, and Factory/registry before coding.
hints.2: LogManager 1—* Logger; Logger—* Appender; Appender→Formatter; parent Logger for hierarchy.
hints.3: Prefer LogManager.getLogger registry + appender list + parent additivity; AsyncAppender as Decorator.

phases.goal: Describe the log pipeline, client API, and a working sync console/file path with level gating.

must_hit.point: Pipeline: Logger.log(level, msg) → level check via getEffectiveLevel → build LogMessage → optional filters → callAppenders (each formats then writes) → bubble to parent if additivity.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks level gate, immutable message, fan-out, format-then-write, optional parent bubble.

must_hit.point: Put the level check before allocating or formatting so disabled DEBUG does not pay String.format / concatenation cost.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Emphasizes ordinal compare and early return before new LogMessage or string work.

must_hit.point: Client API: LogManager.getLogger(name); debug/info/warn/error/fatal; log(level, message); setLevel/addAppender/setAdditivity; LogManager.shutdown to flush and close.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches named getLogger, level helpers, mutators, and shutdown.

must_hit.point: Timed drill target: Logger + LogLevel + ConsoleAppender/FileAppender + level filter + thread-safe writes, then multi-appender list.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Plans a sync console+file demo first, then multi-appender, with async/hierarchy as sketch.

probes: Walk through what happens on logger.info("…") from API call to bytes on disk.
Where exactly do you short-circuit a disabled DEBUG call?

hints.1: Start with sync ConsoleAppender and FileAppender plus a level gate.
hints.2: Effective level check → LogMessage → each appender’s formatter → write.
hints.3: getEffectiveLevel early return; then message; callAppenders; parent if additivity; shutdown flushes.

phases.goal: Show OCP for new sinks/formats and senior extensions like hierarchy, per-appender levels, and remote appenders.

must_hit.point: New Slack/Kafka/DB sink = new LogAppender implementation without editing Logger.log if-else; new JSON vs plain = LogFormatter Strategy swap on the same appender.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds a class implementing LogAppender/LogFormatter; Logger stays closed for modification.

must_hit.point: Named hierarchical loggers with dotted names; child inherits effective level from nearest configured ancestor; additivity=false stops bubble-up to parent appenders.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains parent walk for getEffectiveLevel and additivity controlling propagate.

must_hit.point: Per-appender (or per-destination) thresholds enable console DEBUG with file only WARN—not one global filter only.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Each appender holds its own min level so destinations filter independently.

probes: How do you add a Kafka sink without touching Logger?
How can console be DEBUG while the file appender only accepts WARN?

hints.2: Hierarchy for level inheritance; per-appender min level for multi-threshold.
hints.3: New Appender impl; Formatter Strategy; getEffectiveLevel walk; additivity=false; per-appender threshold.

phases.goal: Ensure thread-safe registry/appender lists, non-interleaved writes, and a sound async/backpressure story.

must_hit.point: Synchronize per appender (or use a single-writer async thread) so one record’s bytes never interleave; use CopyOnWriteArrayList/snapshot for appender lists and ConcurrentHashMap for the logger registry.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects only a global synchronized log() as the long-term answer; locks inside appenders or serializes via one async worker; COW list + concurrent registry.

must_hit.point: Async logging enqueues LogMessage on a bounded BlockingQueue / single-thread executor so callers return fast; name backpressure (drop / block / write-inline when full) and flush on shutdown.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes queue + drain thread or AsyncAppender; policies when full; LogManager.shutdown / shutdown hook.

must_hit.point: Appender failures must not crash the app (catch + fallback stderr/error handler); process exit must not silently lose the async queue.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions try/catch around append and explicit shutdown flush for async.

probes: Two threads log at once and lines garble—where is the race and how do you fix it?
How do you make logging non-blocking, and what happens when the queue is full or the process exits?

hints.1: Shared PrintStream/file handle needs synchronization or a single writer.
hints.2: Per-appender lock or async consumer; concurrent registry; COW appender list.
hints.3: Bounded queue + backpressure policy; shutdown flush; catch appender errors; avoid global lock serializing the whole app.

tradeoffs.topic: Singleton Logger vs Singleton Factory + many named Loggers
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Singleton on Logger blocks per-module levels/appenders (junior smell). Prefer LogManager.getLogger(name) registry so each named logger can have its own level and appenders (CalibreOS senior bar).

tradeoffs.topic: Handler CoR vs list-of-appenders + hierarchy CoR
tradeoffs.strong_answer: INFO→DEBUG→ERROR class chain teaches CoR but is not the Log4j model. Prefer appenders as a fan-out list and hierarchy for level inheritance plus additivity; mention both, implement list+hierarchy.
Sync is correct and simpler for demos; async decouples caller latency but risks loss on crash or a full queue—explicitly name the backpressure policy and shutdown flush.

tradeoffs.topic: Global lock vs per-appender lock / single-writer
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Global synchronized log() is correct but serializes the app; prefer locking inside each appender or one async consumer thread so producers only contend on the queue.

gotchas.trap: Two threads logging at once produce garbled lines on a shared PrintStream or file handle.
gotchas.correction: Synchronize append() per appender or use a single-writer async thread so record bytes never interleave.

gotchas.trap: Assuming one global level filter when the interviewer wants console DEBUG but file only WARN.
gotchas.correction: Use per-appender or per-destination thresholds, not only a single global filter.

gotchas.trap: Adding Slack/Kafka/DB by extending if-else inside Logger.log.
gotchas.correction: Add a new LogAppender implementation; keep Logger closed for modification (OCP).

gotchas.trap: Concatenating strings like "user="+id before the level check.
gotchas.correction: That allocates even when DEBUG is off; prefer lazy or parameterized messages and check level first.

gotchas.trap: An appender throw crashes the application.
gotchas.correction: Catch appender failures and fall back to stderr or an error handler.

gotchas.trap: Process exit drops messages still sitting in the async queue.
gotchas.correction: Register a shutdown hook or call LogManager.shutdown() to flush and close appenders.

gotchas.trap: Making logging non-blocking without defining queue-full and shutdown behavior.
gotchas.correction: Use AsyncAppender Decorator or a shared processor queue; discuss drop vs block vs write-inline when full; flush on shutdown.

gotchas.trap: Named logger com.app should inherit INFO but candidate has no parent walk or additivity control.
gotchas.correction: Parent pointer plus getEffectiveLevel() walk; additivity=false stops bubble-up to parent appenders.
